content.heroDescription: Check whether your microphone works on Windows, PC, Mac, or laptop—and hear how you sound before your WhatsApp, Teams, or Zoom calls. 100% private in-browser testing.
content.deviceHint: Device names stay hidden until you allow access. Access is used only to list devices, then stopped immediately.
content.featuresTitle: Everything you need to check your microphone.
content.featuresDescription: Simple tools for the checks that matter most: is the right mic selected, is it picking up your voice, and does the recording sound usable?

features.title: Real-time waveform
features.desc: See your audio input respond as you speak. A moving waveform confirms that the browser is receiving your microphone signal.

features.title: Choose your device
features.desc: Switch between a built-in mic, USB microphone, webcam, or headset input from the devices available to your browser.

features.title: Hear what others hear
features.desc: Make a short browser recording or use the zero-latency loopback monitor to hear your exact voice, volume, and clarity before your calls.

features.title: Microphone information
features.desc: Review the active sample rate, channel count, and detected device label to help troubleshoot setup issues.

features.title: Permission clarity
features.desc: Clear status messages explain when permission is needed, when the test is running, and when the microphone has stopped.

features.title: Private in your browser
features.desc: The page analyzes the live stream locally. No microphone audio is sent to our server for this test.

content.promo1Title: Want to improve your microphone sound?
content.promo1Desc: Check your positioning, room setup, input selection, and browser permissions before your next call.
content.promo2Desc: Work through the most common permission, connection, and device-selection issues step by step.
content.howTitle: Five seconds to a useful answer.
content.howDesc: You do not need an account or a download. Connect your microphone, allow access, and use the meter and short recording to check it before a Zoom, Teams, Meet, or Discord call.

steps.title: Click the test button
steps.desc: Start the test when you are ready to give this page microphone access.

steps.title: Allow microphone access
steps.desc: Choose Allow in your browser prompt. The browser controls when a site can use your mic.

steps.title: Speak and watch the meter
steps.desc: Say a few words at your normal volume. The level bars should move as you speak.

steps.title: Switch input devices if needed
steps.desc: Use the device list to select your headset, USB microphone, or another available input.

steps.title: Record a short clip
steps.desc: Play the local recording back to check how your voice actually sounds.

content.faqTitle: How do I test my microphone?
content.faqIntro: Find quick answers for how to test a microphone online, on Windows 10 and 11, on a PC, Mac, laptop, Microsoft Teams, or with AirPods.
content.privacyTitle: Your microphone stream stays on this page.
content.privacyDesc: Microphone access starts only after you click the test button and approve the browser prompt. Level analysis and recordings happen locally in your browser. Stop the test when you are done; the page stops its audio tracks and does not upload your recording.
content.footerTagline: A fast, focused microphone checker for calls, recordings, and everyday troubleshooting.
content.footerNote: Made with browser APIs, no upload required.

faqs.a: Click Start microphone test, allow microphone access when your browser asks, and speak normally. The live meter should move as your microphone picks up sound. You can also record a short clip and play it back locally.

faqs.q: How to test if microphone is working?
faqs.a: Start the microphone test, allow browser access, and speak into the microphone. If the level meter responds and a recorded clip plays back clearly, the microphone is working. If there is no signal, check the selected input, mute switch, and device connection.

To test microphone Windows 10, open Settings, choose System, then Sound, and select your microphone under Input to check the input level. You can also use this online microphone test: click Start microphone test, allow access, speak, and confirm that the live meter responds.

To test microphone Windows 11, open Settings, go to System, then Sound, and choose your microphone under Input. Test the signal, or click Start microphone test on this page and speak to see the live level meter respond.

faqs.q: How to test microphone on Mac?
faqs.a: To test microphone on Mac, open System Settings, select Sound, and choose the microphone under Input. You can also use this page to allow browser access, watch the live meter, and play back a short local recording.

faqs.q: How to test microphone on laptop?
faqs.a: Make sure the laptop microphone is not muted, click Start microphone test, and allow access in your browser. Speak at a normal volume and confirm that the level meter moves. If you use a headset or USB microphone, select it from the input device list.

faqs.q: How to test microphone in Teams and Zoom?
faqs.a: Open Microsoft Teams or Zoom Settings, choose Audio/Devices, select your microphone, and run the test call. You can test the same microphone here first by checking the live meter and local recording.

faqs.q: How to test AirPods or wireless microphone?
faqs.a: Connect your AirPods or Bluetooth headset, choose them as the input device, and click Start microphone test. Speak normally and confirm the live meter moves, then record a 5-second clip to hear playback quality.

faqs.q: How do I test my microphone to hear what other people hear?
faqs.a: Connect headphones, click Start microphone test, and turn on the 'Hear myself' loopback monitor. You will hear your voice in real time with zero latency, allowing you to check background noise, echo, and volume balance.

faqs.q: Why is my microphone not working?
faqs.a: Check browser permission, the selected input device, the physical mute switch, and the cable or Bluetooth connection. Close other apps that may be locking the microphone, then reload this page and try again.

faqs.q: Can I test my microphone without uploading audio?
faqs.a: Yes. This microphone test processes the live stream locally in your browser using the Web Audio API. Audio is never sent to any server, and recordings remain completely private on your device.

faqs.q: How do I test my PC microphone locally without opening Windows sound settings?
faqs.a: Open TestYourMicrophone.com in your browser. It uses the Web Audio API to test your microphone locally on your device with a live decibel (dBFS) meter, pitch detector, and instant playback with zero configuration required.

faqs.q: How to test Realtek microphone on Windows?
faqs.a: Select your Realtek microphone or headset in the device list and click Start microphone test. If your volume is quiet, open the Realtek Audio Console to raise the microphone boost slider (+10dB to +20dB) and verify your physical mute switch is off.

faqs.q: How to test microphone using CMD or PowerShell?
faqs.a: Press Win + R, type 'mmsys.cpl' and press Enter to launch Windows Sound control panel from the command line, then speak while watching the green volume meter. For an instant test with real-time dBFS and pitch meters, open TestYourMicrophone.com in your browser.
